operations.what: The worker pins itself to its CPU.
With --count only: the worker opens its counter group.
The worker allocates the buffer and writes every byte of it (first touch).
One untimed pass of the kernel of this interval over the size of this interval.
One-thread runs: the worker reads /proc/self/smaps for its buffers.
One-thread runs: the worker reads four counters of /proc/vmstat.
The worker waits on a barrier until the main thread releases the interval.
The main thread joins the barrier and so releases the worker.

Clock read. The timed interval starts.
operations.where: worker, start of the timed interval

operations.what: Whole passes of the kernel. The old-read sum goes to a volatile variable on the worker stack.
Clock read after at least 8 MiB of reads. The interval ends at the first read at or after --min-ms.
With --count only: one read of the thread CPU clock, then one read of the counter group.
The worker stores its result and waits on the barrier for the main thread.
The main thread joins the barrier. The worker goes on to the warm-up pass of the next interval.
The main thread prints the P row (page state that the worker read before the interval).
The main thread prints the I row and then the T row (and the C row with --count).
The main thread flushes the output. This runs while the worker already does its next warm-up pass.
The returned sum of old read is stored through a pointer to a volatile variable.
The volatile variable is local to the worker.
The 13 entries of the B6 sequence.
Options of every B6 process: 8 MiB, 4 rounds, 300 ms, whole passes.

Start the benchmark process in its own process group.
